compiled_state.description: A change that modifies spend-related configuration (model selection, prompt cache style, retry/context caps, fallback chains, region, LLM provider settings) must fail the Verified CI gate by default; landing it requires an administrator to approve and manually submit the change (same admin-override pattern as the module-size-limit gate). Scope: (1) enumerate the spend-affecting config keys/files (rebar.toml LLM/provider sections and equivalents) and single-source the list; (2) an in-process or operation-linked check that detects a diff touching those keys, per project.portability (CI-only triggers are not portable — provide the local-check fallback, e.g. wired into make verify); (3) CI wiring so the gate fails closed on such diffs with a clear message pointing at the admin-approval path; (4) documentation of the admin approval/submit procedure; (5) tests. Rationale: the Aug 10 caching regression was a spend-affecting config/behavior change that landed with normal review and ran silently for 17 days at material cost (figures in the local-only incident report); changes in this class need a deliberate human decision. Note: this adds a ci_gate mechanism — must carry a mechanism-ok justification per the mechanism-delta ratchet. DEFERRED: implementation blocked until the code review bot is re-enabled (no rebar change can currently land through Gerrit's LLM-Review gate).
compiled_state.title: Gate spend-affecting rebar config changes behind admin approval
